text: Whiteflies on tomato and brinjal are small white insects found on the underside of leaves. Monitor with yellow sticky traps placed at plant height. Remove and destroy heavily infested leaves and control weeds around the field.

text: Leaf curling in brinjal can be caused by sucking pests such as whitefly, aphids or mites. Inspect the underside of young leaves. If many insects are found, contact the local agriculture officer or KVK for the recommended plant protection product and dose.

text: Stem borer in paddy causes dead hearts in the vegetative stage and white ears at flowering. Use light traps to monitor adult moths and remove egg masses from the nursery. Avoid excess nitrogen application.

text: Paddy needs shallow standing water during early growth. Drain the field about one to two weeks before harvest to help uniform ripening.

text: Groundnut prefers well drained sandy loam soil. Waterlogging during pegging and pod development reduces yield. Avoid sowing when heavy rain is forecast in the next two days.

text: Get soil tested before deciding fertilizer. Apply fertilizer in split doses according to the soil test report and local recommendation instead of a single heavy dose.

text: Aphids on tomato are small soft insects clustering on tender shoots and cause leaf curling and sticky honeydew. Encourage natural enemies such as ladybird beetles and avoid unnecessary chemical sprays.

text: Spraying pesticides just before expected rain wastes the product. Check the three day weather forecast and spray in calm, dry conditions in the early morning or late afternoon.
